# 4 Maccabees Chapter 13 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The Brothers' Fraternal Love and Unity

---

**1** I could praise the endurance of those young men all day, and it still would not do them justice. They despised the passions and conquered their torments.

**2** And how do I adequately praise also the magnanimity of the brothers and their noble loyalty to the law?

**3** Like the branches of a tree, which each grow in their own direction yet are one at the root, so these brothers were one in their devotion to the law.

**4** They had been formed in the same law and trained in the same virtues, and so they were bound to one another in deep love.

**5** Their shared nature deepened that love, the law strengthened it, and righteousness made it unbreakable.

**6** The brothers' solidarity gave them courage, so that the tyrant was completely unable to divide them from one another.

**7** The eldest encouraged the others: Be courageous and noble, brothers.

**8** Remember that it was by the same God who created us that the law was given, and that our father Jacob lived by it and proved its truth in his own life.

**9** And the Almighty will not abandon those of us who do not turn away from the commandments of our fathers.

**10** The second said: Be courageous, brothers! We are sons of Abraham and we will not be put to shame in any way.

**11** The third said: Be courageous and noble, brothers — we are fighting the battle of righteousness.

**12** The fourth said: Brothers, do not be afraid of the one who can kill the body but cannot touch the soul.

**13** The fifth said: Brothers, this present time is short and our life is passing away — but the name of those who die for virtue endures forever.

**14** The sixth said: Do not be overcome with grief, brothers. Death is a release from the sufferings of this present life.

**15** And the seventh and youngest said: Brothers, do not be afraid. Take courage — it would not be worthy of people who are ripe in wisdom to fear a man who can only kill the body.

**16** Then each of them, sustained by this reasoning, walked into the flames of torture in full confidence that they would never cease to live.

**17** How extraordinary! What praise is due these noble souls who, having mastered their passions and overcome the fear of death, went willingly to the altar of holy martyrdom!

**18** Did not the mother herself make this brave choice — she who chose the better death for her sons and thereby sealed their immortal victory?

**19** Is she not worthy of the highest praise — she who endured the death of seven sons in a single day and did not allow her spirit to be broken?

**20** For from her womb they came, nurtured in her body, raised by her teaching and her love to endure with virtue — and in her heart she held them even as they died.
